questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In a story, Dad lights a kerosene lamp. Then he hitches the horse to the buggy to go into town for flour. What do these details suggest about the setting?
choices: The story is set a long time ago
The story is set in a modern city
The story is set in outer space
The story is set during a school holiday
questions.explanation: Kerosene lamps and horse buggies were used before electricity and cars were common, so the story is set long ago.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Ned sleeps in a canvas tent near Ballarat in 1853. Each month he pays for a licence so he can dig for gold. What does this setting show about life on the goldfields?
choices: Everyone lived in large brick houses
Many people lived in temporary shelters and had to follow rules
Gold was free and nobody needed permission
Miners travelled to work by train each day
questions.explanation: A tent shows people lived in temporary homes, and the licence shows there were rules about digging for gold.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Lily lives on a cattle station in the outback. Every morning at 9 am she switches on a radio for lessons from a teacher 400 km away. What does this show about her community?
choices: Children in the outback never go to school
Lily's teacher visits the station every day
Children far from towns can learn by radio or distance lessons
Lily's family does not own any animals
questions.explanation: The teacher is very far away, so Lily learns over the radio. This shows how remote communities handle schooling.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In a story set in 1943, Grandma grows vegetables in the backyard and saves her tea and sugar ration coupons. Why would the author include these details?
choices: To show that Grandma likes gardening more than cooking
To show that Grandma was a wealthy shop owner
To show that vegetables were not sold in shops
To show that food was limited during wartime
questions.explanation: Rationing and growing your own food were common in wartime because supplies were short.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Read this line: "I crept down the hall, my heart thumping. Nobody must hear me." Which point of view is the narrator using?
choices: Second person, speaking to the reader as "you"
Third person, as an outsider watching
First person, as the character who is telling the story
Fourth person, as a group of characters
questions.explanation: The word "I" shows the character is telling their own story. That is first person.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Tom tells the story himself: "The referee blew his whistle unfairly. We were robbed!" Why might readers not get the full picture of the game?
choices: Because we only see the game through Tom's own feelings
Because the referee is the real narrator
Because the story is told in the future
Because first person stories never include events
questions.explanation: Tom is upset and tells only his side. Readers cannot be sure the referee really was unfair.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The narrator says: "Zoe smiled at the crowd, but inside she wished she could run away. Her brother thought she looked brave." What does the reader learn from this narrator?
choices: Zoe is not nervous at all
Zoe is hiding her nerves, and her brother does not know
Zoe's brother is the one telling the story
Zoe's brother is also feeling nervous
questions.explanation: The narrator knows what Zoe really feels, so readers learn something her brother misses.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A story told in the first person lets readers know the narrator's own thoughts and feelings directly.
questions.explanation: The narrator is a character telling their own story, so they can share what they think and feel.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A poet writes: "Her smile was a sunrise over the bay." What does this metaphor suggest about her smile?
choices: It was bright, warm and welcoming
It happened very early in the morning
It was cold and hard to see
It happened near the beach
questions.explanation: A sunrise brings light and warmth. Saying her smile is a sunrise shows it made everything feel bright.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A poem says: "The snake slithered silently, sliding sideways through the scrub." Why does the poet repeat the s sound so often?
choices: To make the snake seem noisy and angry
To make the line sound like a snake hissing and moving
To show that the snake is very large
To make the poem rhyme at the end
questions.explanation: Repeating the s sound is called alliteration. It sounds like hissing, which suits a sneaking snake.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which of these sentences contains a simile?
choices: The classroom was a zoo at lunchtime.
The sun smiled down on the oval.
Thunder grumbled over the hills.
The ball was as round as a full moon.
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using "as" or "like". The ball is compared to the moon using "as round as".
